parsed.explanation: The operative regime criminalises trans identity itself: the passed 2026 bill, awaiting assent that is 'widely expected', carries up to three years for identifying as LGBTQ, longer terms for advocacy, crossdressing provisions, and a duty to report — converting neighbours, staff and hosts into outing vectors. Existing law criminalises 'unnatural carnal knowledge'; mob violence against perceived LGBT people is documented; there is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination protection, and community infrastructure is raided and closed, forcing groups underground. No enforcement record exists yet for the 2026 bill, and whether the identification offence reaches short-term visitors is unresolved — but the identity-only offence plus duty-to-report is a state threat-framing far beyond sexuality-law-only jurisdictions, and recourse is thin. Severity (imprisonment) is high; current frequency is low pending signature.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented trans-specific entry, visa or airport screening rule; whether the identification or crossdressing offence applies to visitors is unresolved, so border exposure is an open question rather than a documented practice.
entry_documents.interaction: If assented, an outed visitor at any later stage (hotel, hospital, police check) becomes criminally exposed under national law; no border mechanism documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Existing 3-year 'unnatural carnal knowledge' statute; the 2026 bill adds identity offence, longer promotion terms and a duty to report; no prison-placement rule for trans prisoners is documented, and mob justice against perceived LGBT people is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A paralegal initiative defends LGBTQ people in court — thin, unquantified recourse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Duty-to-report channels residents and potentially hosts/police toward investigation of outed visitors; custody conditions for trans detainees undocumented.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; no shelter provision exists for residents, signalling absent service infrastructure.
care_services.interaction: Medication continuity and emergency-care treatment of an outed trans visitor are undocumented open questions in a criminalising regime.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing is explicit: identity itself criminalised, crossdressing criminalised, promotion criminalised, duty to report. Religious and political leaders closed community centres; national security raided a rights office; the 2026 passage attributed to religious pressure.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Supreme court entertained challenges but deferred review until assent; petitions dismissed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Legal channels have consistently failed to block the statute; the 2024 version lapsed but was reintroduced and passed again.

minors_guardians.exposure: Conversion therapy by religious groups is documented (family-initiated for residents); whether the criminal framework reaches a minor travelling with a trans parent is undocumented, but hostile climate creates outing and separation risk for travelling families.
minors_guardians.interaction: No specific rule touching travelling minors or guardians appears in the record.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Mob justice against perceived LGBT people is documented; blackmail and violence linked to evictions and suicides among residents. Visitor-facing street-violence prevalence is not separately documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Paralegal court support; police response to anti-trans violence not documented as protective.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin-data: dated (2017–2018) violence documentation, weak evidence about present frequency either way.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection, no legal gender recognition; community operates secretly; self-censorship and panic reported. Unresolved whether offences bind visitors; no enforcement record yet for the 2026 bill.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Paralegal initiative and (before closure) community infrastructure; both marginal.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Assent expected imminently could activate the identity offence nationwide with no working remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Caldera criminalises conduct applied selectively with blackmail and prosecution; this dossier is worse in kind — it criminalises identity and crossdressing with a duty to report — but its enforcement record is not yet established, and imprisonment outcomes beyond the old 3-year statute are undocumented. Slightly above 0.25-D, not much.

Drellia's registration database durably exposes visitors but charges are uncommon and lethal punishment not credible. Here the threat-framing is harsher (identity criminalised, mob justice documented), yet documented visitor-facing enforcement is thinner. Comparable exposure tier, slightly below 0.45-D.

Vellmaris shows national equality law reliably restraining officer conduct and working remedies. This jurisdiction has the inverse: no protections, closed community infrastructure, and a passed criminalisation statute — a clear tier below 0.65-A.

Varnalia documents routine arrests, custodial beatings and illusory remedies today. This dossier documents no current enforcement against visitors, and its 3-year penalty tier is lower; it sits above 0.15-A on present evidence.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a criminalising state whose new statute — passed, assent expected — targets trans identity itself with imprisonment, crossdressing bans and a duty to report that mobilises the population as outing agents, atop an existing sodomy statute, documented mob violence, no legal recognition and no anti-discrimination recourse. Civil-society and judicial channels have failed to block it; community infrastructure has been forcibly closed. The traveller-facing open questions (application to visitors, border screening, custody practice, care access) and the absence of enforcement record under the new bill hold the score above the 0.15 tier, but the severity-if-outed — criminal identity offence, imprisonment, hostile street and state climate — places it firmly in the High Risk band around 0.28.
